knowledgePattern: Transform signed integral intervals and eliminate overlapping pieces

hints.title: Track the input intervals
hints.body: For each transformed function, list which original input values correspond to the two displayed endpoints.
hints.recap: Horizontal transformations move inputs; a reflection reverses their order without changing graph heights.
hints.pitfall: A transformed interval is not necessarily the same as the displayed integration limits.
hints.pause: Match each integral to an interval of the original graph.

recall.reminder: Horizontal transformations move inputs; a reflection reverses their order without changing graph heights.

hints.title: Account for widths
hints.body: A horizontal stretch or compression multiplies every strip width by the same factor, so it multiplies signed area by that factor too.
hints.recap: Input transformations and signed area must be tracked together.
hints.pitfall: Keep the compression factor separate from the transformed endpoints.
hints.pause: Convert all conditions into signed integrals of f itself.

recall.reminder: Input transformations and signed area must be tracked together.

hints.title: Separate adjacent pieces
hints.body: Name the integrals over the adjacent intervals separated by the endpoints you found. Express each condition as a sum of those pieces.
hints.recap: Elimination can isolate one shared unknown from several linear conditions.
hints.pitfall: The same overlapping strip must represent the same unknown in every condition.
hints.pause: Eliminate the unwanted pieces to obtain the requested integral.

recall.reminder: Elimination can isolate one shared unknown from several linear conditions.

solution:
1. For f(x+1), inputs run from 1 to 3 without changing widths. Thus ∫13f(x)dx=1. For f(2−x) on [0,2], the graph is reflected horizontally within the same interval, preserving signed area, so ∫02f(x)dx=2.

2. The graph of f(2x) has half the horizontal widths of f. Inputs from 0 to 3/2 correspond to original inputs from 0 to 3. Consequently ∫03f(x)dx=2·3=6.

3. Put A=∫01f, B=∫12f, C=∫23f. We have B+C=1, A+B=2, and A+B+C=6.

4. Adding the first two equations and subtracting the third leaves B=1+2−6=−3. Answer B. A signed integral may be negative; no positivity of f is stated.
